subject: DataForge — privatenet hosting path selection and egress IP asks
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (hosting paths & network asks)

Alex — thanks again for the conversation earlier today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can keep momentum toward a POC: 

Summary of your preferences from the call:
- DataForge is leaning toward a Private VPC deployment for regulatory isolation (SOC2 + regional data residency).
- Primary questions: PrivateLink vs VPC peering, static egress IPs (for vendor allowlists), and timeline for a network workshop + test tenant.

What Redwood recommends (high level):
- PrivateLink (recommended) when customers prefer minimal routing changes and want control over inbound allowlists; this uses AWS/GCP Private Service Connect endpoints.
- VPC peering when you need low-latency, full-L3 connectivity and route advertising between subnets (requires updates to route tables).
- Dedicated (reserved) capacity is an alternative if you want predictable throughput without changing network topology, but it doesn't provide the same tenant isolation as a Private VPC.

Network asks for your team to confirm (please reply inline):
1) Hosting path preference: PrivateLink or VPC peering?
2) If PrivateLink: does your security team require our service endpoints to be included in an IP allowlist, or will DNS-based allowlisting via the endpoint suffice?
3) Egress: do you need a fixed set of static outbound IPs for Redwood-originated egress (for third-party vendors), or will egress originate from your VPC (you manage outbound)?
4) Ports/protocols: do you have an allowlist of destination ports (HTTPS 443 is typical; any additional ports?)
5) Target date for a network workshop / ops sync (we suggest 1 week to collect artifacts, 2-3 weeks to do a staged POC).

Attached: Redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf (high-level checklist we discussed). Also happy to produce a connectivity diagram once you confirm hosting path.

Next step from our side: Vivek (SE) will propose two network designs and default egress IP ranges once you confirm PrivateLink vs Peering.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman

Thanks Naomi — good recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Hosting path: initial preference is PrivateLink because our infra team does not want new peering relationships across accounts. If there are limits with PrivateLink (performance or port restrictions) we can revisit.

- IP allowlist: Security prefers IP-based allowlists for outbound vendors. For inbound, if PrivateLink gives us a stable endpoint DNS + certificate, that might be okay for our app-to-service traffic.

- Egress: we have two egress concerns: (1) Redwood-originated callbacks to third-party vendors (they require fixed IPs on their side), and (2) DataForge-originated egress from our VPC (we control that). Can Redwood provide a set of static egress IPs for callbacks originating from Redwood systems? If not, what are recommended mitigations?

- Ports: HTTPS (443) only for the POC.

- Timeline: we can do a network workshop next Thursday (2026-06-17) at 10am PT if that works for your team. We'll have netops + security on the call.

Alex — great questions, thank you. Short answers and what we'll prepare for the workshop: 

PrivateLink vs VPC peering (practical):
- PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink / GCP PSC): inbound traffic arrives over a service endpoint in your VPC. Pros: no route-table changes, minimal blast radius, DNS-based endpoint (you call a customer-specific FQDN). Cons: you won't see our internal host IPs directly; if a third party requires our IPs for their allowlist, that is the key ask.
- VPC peering: offers full L3 adjacency. Pros: direct routing and simpler IP-based allowlisting. Cons: requires route table and possibly security policy changes at your infra team.

Egress IPs and callbacks (the critical piece you highlighted):
- Option A (Redwood-managed static egress): For Private tenant deployments we can publish a small set of static egress NAT IPs per-region that our control plane uses for callbacks to vendor endpoints. That is the path we recommend if third parties require fixed allowlists. There is an operational step: we assign and reserve those NAT IPs and share them with you ahead of POC.
- Option B (Customer-managed egress): If your VPC keeps outbound traffic, you control egress IPs; Redwood-originated callbacks can be routed back into your VPC and then egress from there. This requires peering or PrivateLink with appropriate route targets.

For the workshop we will bring: a) a sample connectivity diagram for both PrivateLink and peering setups, b) a proposed list of 6 static NAT egress IPs (per-region) for you to review, c) a short checklist of IAM/network permissions we need to validate.

Action items for DataForge (if you can deliver before the workshop):
- Placeholder network diagram or VPC ids (we can accept a sanitized diagram).
- Security contact email for the workshop (Sarah listed above).
- Any hard vendor IPs that must be reached by Redwood callbacks.

We'll target the workshop on Thu, 2026-06-17 10:00 PT as Alex suggested. Priyom, can you draft the sample IP list and two diagrams (PrivateLink vs Peering) by EOD Wednesday (6/10)?

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
